description: An empty JSON array, presented under each of the nine recognised artifact filenames. Under gitleaks.json it ROUTES -- a bare top-level array is that tool's whole envelope, and an empty one is a legitimate clean report -- and under the other eight it halts. It is the control that keeps the envelope check from becoming an emptiness check.
outcome: mixed -- one routing decision and eight halts
null_field_note: tool, scanner_class and adapter are null here because this file describes nine routings rather than one: the per-name table below carries the tool, the shape and the adapter for the name that routes, and the halt reason for the eight that do not. adapter_invoked is false for all nine -- the routing decision names an adapter by string key, and this test asserts over the decision without calling it.

fixture.authored_note: Authored, not captured. It is the emptiest well-formed array a runner could leave behind. Nothing in it is a finding, a secret, a credential or a token, and it names no path, so no location of any kind is characterised by it.
fixture.why_this_document: An over-strict router is as wrong as a permissive one, and it fails in the opposite direction: it would halt on a tool that legitimately found nothing. AAP 0.5.4 makes an empty report ordinary -- the count unit is walked and yields zero records, and the reconciliation identity 0 = 0 + 0 holds over an artifact that was present and traversed, which is a different thing entirely from an artifact that was absent. This fixture is what pins that distinction at the router.
fixture.the_pair_it_completes: Its sibling halt-shape-empty-object.json is equally empty and halts under all nine names. Same emptiness, different container, opposite outcome under gitleaks.json -- so the two together establish that the check keys on the envelope AAP 0.5.4's per-shape table names and not on whether anything is inside it.

field_order_authority: harness/lib/normalize/emit.py, the FIELDS constant. Recorded for parity with the positive expected files in this folder; no row below carries it, because rows is empty by expectation.

shape_detection.conjunction: isinstance(doc, Mapping) and doc.get("version") == "2.1.0" and isinstance(doc.get("runs"), list)
shape_detection.is_sarif_derivation: The document is a list rather than a mapping, so the first condition fails and the conjunction is False. This is the sharpest subject in the folder for that first condition: a detector that skipped the isinstance check and called .get on the document would raise AttributeError here rather than return False, and an exception from the detector is a different failure from a correct negative.

container_check.note: The top level is a JSON array, which IS a supported container -- two of the nine artifacts are array-topped -- so REASON_UNSUPPORTED_DOCUMENT_TYPE does not apply under any name.

native_shape_detection.conclusion: matches gitleaks' envelope and no other tool's
native_shape_detection.authority: shape._NATIVE_ENVELOPE in harness/lib/normalize/shape.py, one entry per canonical tool, each pairing the predicate the router enforces with the prose the halt quotes.
native_shape_detection.checks_note: Exactly one verdict is True. gitleaks' envelope is a top-level JSON array and nothing more, because its records carry no envelope of their own -- the artifact IS the array. Checkov's array form is refused: it requires a non-empty array whose every element is a report object carrying a results object, and an empty array establishes nothing about its elements, so admitting it would let a document with no report at all route as Checkov's. The six mapping-topped envelopes are refused by type before any key is read, and the three SARIF producers are refused by construction.
native_shape_detection.why_checkovs_array_form_needs_the_non_em: Recorded because it is the one asymmetry in the table and it is deliberate. gitleaks' marker is the container itself, so an empty container is a complete, legitimate report. Checkov's marker is the elements' shape, so an empty array carries no marker -- it is indistinguishable from gitleaks' empty report, from an empty OSV array and from an arbitrary empty list. Requiring one report object is what keeps the two array-topped envelopes distinguishable, and the cost is named rather than hidden: a Checkov run that produced a truly empty multi-framework array halts, and it halts with the envelope quoted, which is a stated outcome a reader can act on rather than a silent zero.
native_shape_detection.envelope_only_note: What the router checks is the envelope and only the envelope. Under gitleaks.json this document routes, and every judgement about what the array holds -- including that it holds nothing -- belongs to the adapter and to the reconciliation identity, not to the router.

under_each_recognised_name.envelope: a SARIF 2.1.0 document -- version == "2.1.0" together with a runs array; this runner writes SARIF and nothing else, so there is no native shape to fall back to
a SARIF 2.1.0 document -- version == "2.1.0" together with a runs array; this runner writes SARIF and nothing else, so there is no native shape to fall back to
a SARIF 2.1.0 document -- version == "2.1.0" together with a runs array; this runner writes SARIF and nothing else, so there is no native shape to fall back to
a JSON array of finding objects at the top level (an empty array is a legitimate clean report)
either one report object carrying a 'results' object, or a non-empty top-level array of such report objects (the multi-framework form)
a report object carrying 'Results', as an array or null (an empty or null 'Results' is a legitimate clean report, but the key's absence means the document is not a Trivy report)
a report object carrying an 'results' array
a report object carrying a 'dependencies' array (an empty array is a legitimate clean report)
a collector object carrying a 'findings' array, as written by harness/lib/joern-scan.sc

under_each_recognised_name_note: Nine entries, one per artifact filename, in canonical tool order. One routes and eight halt, and the split is the whole point of the fixture: the router refuses a document that is not the named tool's shape, and accepts one that is, whether or not it carries records.

under_its_own_name.note: The name is not one of the nine, so resolve_tool returns None and the name reason is attributed before any envelope is consulted. Recorded for completeness; this fixture's purpose is the claimed-name table above.

routed_outcome_under_gitleaks.adapter_boundary: The routing decision names the gitleaks adapter by string key; this file asserts the decision and stops there. What that adapter does with an empty array is its own module's business and is asserted in oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/test_gitleaks_adapter.py, so no expectation about rows is recorded here and none is implied.
routed_outcome_under_gitleaks.why_it_must_not_halt: A halt here would stop the run over a tool that ran correctly and found nothing. That is the over-strict failure, and it is not harmless either: it would make a clean artifact unprocessable and put the router in the business of judging results, which AAP 0.3.2 forbids in every direction.

halt.expected_under: eight of the nine recognised artifact filenames
halt.raised_before: any adapter module is named, imported or called, and before any record traversal of any kind
halt.reason_note: shape.py names four reasons. The top level is a supported container and each of the nine names resolves, so neither the container reason nor the name reason applies; the eight halts split between the producer reason and the native-envelope reason exactly as the per-name table records.

observed_attributes.artifact_path_note: Whatever subject the caller passed, echoed unchanged. The negative test passes the claimed artifact filename, so no absolute path appears anywhere in this file.
observed_attributes.stem: the canonical tool identifier the claimed name resolved to
observed_attributes.version_note: None because shape.describe_document reads a version only from a mapping; an array has no keys to read one from, and the attribute records that absence rather than inventing a value.
observed_attributes.expectation: the prose statement of what that tool's artifact must be, non-empty for each of the eight refusing names

halt.authority: AAP 0.5.4 -- an artifact matching neither the SARIF shape nor a known native shape is a halt rather than a best-effort parse -- and AAP 0.9.2, which lists it among the conditions that stop the run.

not_a_rejection.reject_classes_authority: harness/lib/normalize/paths.py, the REJECT_CLASSES tuple -- a closed set of ten class names, not copied here so the one authority cannot drift into two.
not_a_rejection.statement: The stated outcome is a halt, not a counted rejection: "halt", "UnknownArtifactShape" and each of the four halt reasons shape.py names are provably absent from paths.REJECT_CLASSES, and the test asserts that non-membership programmatically rather than by inspection. A rejection is a per-record outcome inside an adapter that already owns the artifact; this document never reaches an adapter, so there is no record to reject and nothing to count under any class.

parse.note: The fixture is well-formed JSON and json.load succeeds on it. Malformed input is a different condition, owned by the reject-*-malformed-record fixtures.

counts.reconciliation_identity: not asserted by this fixture -- eight names halt before any traversal, and under gitleaks.json this file's expectation stops at the routing decision

counts_note: Null rather than 0 for the raw fields, and the reason is different from its sibling's. For the eight halting names there is no count unit to walk. For gitleaks.json there is one -- the array itself -- but walking it is the adapter's and the reconciliation's work, not the router's, so recording a number here would be recording a measurement this file did not make.
rows_note: Empty because no adapter is invoked under any of the nine names. Under gitleaks.json a legitimate empty artifact would also produce no row, and the two emptinesses must not be conflated: this file's zero is "nothing was built", not "the artifact held nothing".
row_derivations_note: Empty because no row exists to derive.
guarded_failure: Two failures are guarded at once, in opposite directions. A router keying on the filename alone would accept this array under all nine names, and the Trivy, Checkov, Dependency-Check, OSV-Scanner and Joern adapters would each iterate a document with none of their containers and report zero rows -- silent, and indistinguishable from a clean scan. A router that treated emptiness itself as suspicious would halt under gitleaks.json and stop the run over a tool that ran correctly and found nothing. Only the envelope test produces the right answer in both directions.

assertions: shape.route over this document under gitleaks.json returns a RoutingDecision whose shape is native, whose tool is gitleaks and whose adapter is the gitleaks module key -- it does not raise.
shape.route over this document under each of the other eight artifact filenames raises shape.UnknownArtifactShape, with the reason the per-name table records for that name.
shape.matches_native_shape is True for gitleaks and False for the other eight tools over this document.
The halts carry top_level_type "array", python_type "list", version None, an empty key list, length 0, sarif_detected False and a non-empty expectation.
shape.is_sarif over the document is False and does not raise, which is the assertion the array top level exists to exercise.
No adapter is invoked by any of the nine routing calls, including the one that routes: the decision names an adapter by string key and imports none.
Neither the outcome nor any halt reason is a member of paths.REJECT_CLASSES.
negative_test_contract.mandated_direction_note: The mandated direction -- a native artifact must not route to the SARIF adapter -- is owned by the same test file over the native fixtures. This fixture adds the control that keeps the strictness those assertions require from being satisfied by a router that refuses everything: a router that halted on every document would pass every negative assertion in this file and fail this one.

related_fixtures.sibling_container: oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/halt-shape-empty-object.json -- the same emptiness in the other container, which no envelope admits.
related_fixtures.captured_array_topped_artifact: oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/gitleaks.json -- the captured artifact whose envelope this document satisfies, with records in it.
related_fixtures.checkov_array_form: oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/checkov-alt-shape.json -- the non-empty multi-framework array, which is what Checkov's array-form envelope requires and what this document is not.
related_fixtures.note: Named so a reader can see which layer owns which failure. No fixture's outcome is inferred from another's.

behaviours_not_exercised_by_this_fixture: Row construction of any kind -- no adapter runs under any of the nine names.
Path resolution -- normalize.paths is never called.
Per-record rejection -- none of the ten classes in paths.REJECT_CLASSES is reachable from a routing decision or a shape halt.
REASON_UNSUPPORTED_DOCUMENT_TYPE, which needs a top level that is neither a JSON object nor a JSON array; an array is one of the two.
The valid-SARIF-under-an-unexpected-name halt, whose sarif_detected attribute is True; this document's is False.
What the gitleaks adapter does with an empty array, which test_gitleaks_adapter.py owns.
An adapter's own record-level validation and its own halt.
Malformed JSON, owned by the reject-*-malformed-record fixtures.
The reconciliation identity, which this file records no measurement for.
how_to_check_this_file: Parse the fixture and compare its sha256 and byte size against the fixture block; it holds exactly [] and a trailing newline. Read shape._NATIVE_ENVELOPE and confirm gitleaks' predicate is a bare top-level-array test while Checkov's array form requires a non-empty array of report objects, then read route and confirm a satisfied envelope returns a decision and an unsatisfied one raises. Then run the negative test: every assertion in negative_test_contract is checkable from this file alone.
prohibitions_observed: No secret value, credential, token or redacted-secret placeholder appears in any field of this file (the tree is committed to git). No finding is judged -- nothing here is called real, important, a false positive or a duplicate. Nothing is deduplicated. No tool's output is characterised against another's: this file describes one document's shape detection and the outcomes it must produce, and nothing else.
